newsitem.title: UK: East European 1996/97 sugar output seen lower -Man.
newsitem.headline: East European 1996/97 sugar output seen lower -Man.

text.p: Eastern Europe's sugar production from the 1996/97 beet crop should total 8.46 million tonnes white value, 458,000 tonnes lower than in the previous crop year, trade house E D & F Man said on Tuesday. The forecast was marginally lower than Man's first production estimate, released in September.
Improved crop prospects in Poland, where production was expected to 2.05 million tonnes, would counterbalance further reductions in key producers Russia and Ukraine, it said.
Man reduced its forecast for Russian sugar production by 50,000 tonnes to 1.7 million tonnes, adding that there might be further room for adjustment on the downside.

Bad weather and lack of working machinery in Russia had hampered the progress of the harvest, while beet yields were reported to be significantly lower than last season, it said. Prospects for the Ukrainian crop were also bleak. Man cut its 1996/97 production forecast to 2.8 million tonnes, the level recently mentioned by the country's deputy prime minister, after its previous estimate of 2.9 million tonnes. "In Ukraine the harvest is also well behind last year but it did start two weeks later in the hope that it would give the beets more time to mature," Man said.
But beet yields were lower and harvesting was slow, it said.
